The central question is whether these sinks represent genuine information routing — encoder positions that are actually most predictive of likely decoder outputs across the training distribution — or whether they represent a degenerate attentional shortcut that the model has learned because gradient signal from cross-entropy loss can be satisfied without attending to the bulk of the encoder sequence. The practical stakes are high in retrieval-augmented generation and long-document summarization, where the model's apparent fluency masks systematic failures to integrate distal encoder context.

Critically, the frozen encoder failure mode is length-ratio dependent in a different direction from the sink case: because frozen encoder representations at pretraining were never exposed to extreme compression targets, the key-value geometry at distal encoder positions is actually richer than in finetuned encoders (no co-adaptation degradation occurred), but the decoder cannot exploit this richness because its query projections have insufficient capacity to navigate a key-value space that wasn't organized around summarization-relevant features, causing systematic neglect of mid-document encoder positions that are neither positionally privileged nor pretraining-salient.
